data.narrative:
Kyoto Fusioneering is a Series C nuclear energy company that has raised $125M+ to date. The valuation universe comprises 10 comparable companies across the sector: 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private companies including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Last Energy.

Only one valuation method proved applicable to this analysis. The stage-progression approach uses the $125M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $212M. The peer-median method was not applicable: while the nuclear energy sector contains four comparable companies, none met the threshold of three or more datapoints within the same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier, making a narrow-set median unreliable. A broader sector median would conflate companies with materially different risk profiles and capital structures.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $181M (low) to $244M (high), with a median of $212M. This range reflects the mechanics of stage-progression alone and carries meaningful uncertainty given the method's reliance on a single comparable basis. The key limitation is the insufficient narrow peer set in nuclear energy at this valuation tier and stage, which constrains triangulation depth. Further precision would require either additional same-stage private comps or materialized public market data from comparable nuclear fission developers.
